ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-04-17, accession 0001193125-26-161714): the registered NYSE security is American Depositary Shares 'each representing 10 Series B shares' (20-F cover / Description of Securities), and the EPS disclosure states 'Earnings per ADS are based on a ratio of 10 Series B shares per ADS'

capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for fiscal years 2022, 2023, 2024 of the last 3 under every tag the engine reads: EDGAR companyfacts for this IFRS filer carries no PurchaseOfPropertyPlantAndEquipment (or any capex) concept at all, because the filer's capex is concession-asset investment reported on this single combined cash-flow line. The engine applies one override value to every missing period; Ps.10,444,346,000 is the filed FY2023 figure, and FY2023 is the median year of the 3-year normalized base once capex is charged at filed values (filed-basis OE/share: FY2022 $0.4113, FY2023 $0.4077, FY2024 $0.8425 per ordinary share), so the scored base is built from the exact filed figure for its year. The single value overstates FY2024 capex (filed Ps.7,845m) and understates nothing in the base year; FY2025's filed Ps.12,397m shows the MDP capex cycle is rising, not falling, so the override is not flattering the forward picture. Declared in MXN, the reporting currency; the engine FX-converts at each period-end rate.
capex_override.source: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (filed 2025-04-24, accession 0000950170-25-057571), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities: 'Purchases of machinery, equipment, improvements on leased assets, improvements to concession assets and advance payments to suppliers' Ps.8,431,106 thousand for FY2022, Ps.10,444,346 thousand for FY2023 and Ps.7,844,983 thousand for FY2024 (in thousands of Mexican pesos); the same line in the FY2025 20-F (filed 2026-04-17) is Ps.10,444,346 thousand FY2023 / Ps.7,844,983 thousand FY2024 / Ps.12,396,949 thousand FY2025, confirming the series

moat_against: Finite concessions: Mexican concessions expire 2048 (~22 years) and concession assets revert — a perpetuity terminal value assumes renewal the filing does not grant

Regulator sets the ceiling: five-year MDP reviews reset maximum tariffs and impose the capex program (Ps.43,185m committed 2025-2029 in Mexico); the 2025-2029 bases added a claw-back on excess workload units
Traffic cyclicality: Mexican workload units fell in 2024 (-1.7%) after +10.5% in 2023, and FY2020 revenue fell ~27% in MXN on COVID
MXN earnings vs a USD ADS price: the peso fell ~18% against the USD at the 2024 period-end ECB rate vs 2023, mechanically cutting USD owner's earnings
Mandatory MDP capex is the owner's-earnings story: the purchases-of-concession-assets line jumped to Ps.12,397m in FY2025, cutting filing-basis OE/share ~34% in MXN in one year
moat_for: Sole-operator concessions: 12 Mexican airports (Guadalajara, Tijuana, Puerto Vallarta, Los Cabos + 8) to 2048 and 2 Jamaican airports — no competing airport in each catchment
Regulated pricing power proven in the 2025-2029 tariff reset: weighted average maximum tariffs +18.1% in 2025, with PPI indexation inside each five-year MDP period
ROIC well above the cost of capital through a cycle: roic_proxy 17.8% even in COVID-year FY2020, 49.5% FY2023, 37.7% FY2024 (fundamentals.json); ROE 36-46% FY2022-24
High and stable cash margins: EBITDA margin ex-IFRIC-12 67.1% in 2Q25 (66.8% 2Q24) in company reporting
Non-aeronautical diversification (retail, cargo/bonded warehouses via GWTC consolidated Jul 2024) growing faster than aeronautical and less traffic-sensitive
moat_justification: Regulated local-monopoly airport concessions: GAP is the sole operator of 12 Mexican airports (Guadalajara, Tijuana, Puerto Vallarta, Los Cabos and 8 others) under 50-year concessions to 2048 plus 2 Jamaican airports, with maximum tariffs reset every five years under the Master Development Program framework and adjusted for Mexican PPI. Returns prove the franchise: fundamentals.json roic_proxy was 13.5% (FY2015), 26.4% (FY2018), 30.1% (FY2019), still 17.8% in the COVID trough (FY2020), 42.1% (FY2021), 64.8% (FY2022), 49.5% (FY2023) and 37.7% (FY2024) — above the cost of capital through a full cycle including a traffic collapse; ROE ran 36-46% in FY2022-24 and the ex-IFRIC-12 EBITDA margin was 67.1% in 2Q25 company reporting. Gross margin is not presented in the filing (no cost-of-sales split), so the moat rests on ROIC/ROE and margin evidence instead. Capped at 7, not higher: the concessions are finite (Mexican concessions expire 2048 and assets revert), the regulator sets the tariff ceiling and the mandated capex program (Ps.43,185m committed for the Mexican airports in the 2025-2029 MDP), traffic is cyclical, and earnings are MXN-denominated. CAP = 2 + 1.3 x 7 = 11.1 years.
name: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V. (Pacific Airport Group)
one_liner: Regulated airport-concession monopoly, moat 7/10 - but at $203.90 the ADS prices in a growth path the mandated capex cycle cannot deliver: weighted IRR 5.56% (band D to D, even super-bull 9.12%), weighted IV@15% $45.00 on a $4.08/ADS normalized OE base (2.0% OE yield); clears 15% only below ~$45.

sbc_override.source: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-04-17, accession 0001193125-26-161714), Item 16G NYSE-standards comparison, Equity Compensation Plans: 'No equity-compensation plans have been approved by our shareholders'; Note 22 Employee Cost for 2023, 2024 and 2025 is comprised solely of wages and salaries, other remunerations, social benefits, severance payments, labor union fees, taxes on employee benefits, PTU and retirement benefits — no share-based line; the term 'share-based' appears nowhere in the 20-F, and EDGAR companyfacts carries no ifrs-full AdjustmentsForSharebasedPayments fact for this filer in any year

shares_override.ack_reason: Out of band by construction against the filed series: the companyfacts WeightedAverageShares value (505,277,464,000) is the filer's count scaled 1,000x, so the correct filing count of 505,277,464 sits at 0.001x of the filed value, outside the 0.1x-10x band. The value is not an estimate — it is the count printed in the 20-F EPS disclosure and proven by the filer's own EPS arithmetic (attributable profit / diluted EPS = 505.28m).
shares_override.reason: DATA_GAP:shares — DILUTED shares missing for fiscal years 2022, 2023, 2024 of the last 3; the only filed count is ifrs-full WeightedAverageShares, a basic tag, and companyfacts carries it scaled 1,000x (505,277,464,000) because the filing presents share counts alongside statements in thousands — the same share-basis defect family as NTNX/VIV/DD in this sweep. The filer's own EPS note states basic and diluted are the same (no potentially dilutive shares), so the basic count IS the diluted count. The engine applies this single FY2023-25 value to every missing period; for FY2022 it uses a 0.6% smaller denominator than the filer's own 508,371,309 (immaterial, disclosed), and it is exact for FY2023 and FY2024, two of the three base years.
shares_override.source: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-04-17, accession 0001193125-26-161714), EPS disclosure: weighted average common shares outstanding (excluding treasury shares) of 519,372,684 (FY2021), 508,371,309 (FY2022), 505,277,464 (FY2023), 505,277,464 (FY2024) and 505,277,464 (FY2025), reflecting the repurchase program; accounting policy note r: 'The Company does not have any potentially diluted shares; and therefore, basic and diluted earnings per share are the same' (also in the FY2024 20-F). Cross-check from companyfacts: FY2024 profit attributable to owners Ps.8,612,157 thousand / filed diluted EPS Ps.17.0444 = 505.28 million shares
